annotation.title_clean: Forms of Robot Liability: Criminal Robots and Corporate Criminal Responsibility
annotation.title_en: Forms of Robot Liability: Criminal Robots and Corporate Criminal Responsibility
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Book chapter on the responsibility gap when robots cause harm. It argues robots cannot currently be criminally punished or held as criminals, but corporate responsibility, including criminal liability where recognized, can be extended to harm caused by corporation-controlled robots, requiring at least negligence in programming, testing or supervision.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots cannot at present be coherently or practically subjected to criminal punishment.
Traditional corporate criminal responsibility rules do not capture harm from robots' autonomous acts.
Corporate responsibility can in principle be extended to harm caused by corporation-controlled robots.
Corporate liability should not be unlimited and should require negligence in programming, testing or supervising.
Special 'Robot CCR' applies only when harm cannot be traced to a human source.
